To ensure the registry's integrity and availability during recovery, I have finalized the implementation details for handling discrepancies, epoch management, idempotency, and audit-log event delivery.

I will consolidate the proposed controls into a prioritized recovery-drill plan with the following key components:
1. Restore test with append-only changes and comparison against independently retained checkpoints.
2. Recovery fence with a new registry epoch or generation token.
3. Independent recovery of the status table's event log and checkpoints.
4. Verification of the event log against signed checkpoints or hash-chain anchors.
5. Compare-and-swap operation for promotion against the live log head.
6. Designation of a specific individual or role for the recovery drill's go/no-go decision.
7. Gradual traffic ramp-up and monitoring after recovery, with a maximum allowed rate of 100 events per second and a ramp-up period of 30 minutes, which will not count toward the RTO.

The drill will test the most uncertain recovery assumption regarding the independence and freshness of the recovery log and checkpoints. The pass/fail criteria will be based on:
- Ability to access the recovery log and checkpoints within 1 hour.
- Absence of shared control-plane dependencies.
- Freshness of the accepted checkpoint, defined as being within 24 hours of the current time, with a separate verified replay source able to recover the intervening events.
- Successful rebuild of the status-table projection with verified log high-water mark and matching watermark.

The recovery objectives are defined as follows:
- Recovery Time Objective (RTO) for read-only service: 1 hour (proposed target; actual capability to be verified during the drill), measured from the controlled failure injection to sustained availability of read-only service with required checks passing, sustained for at least 5 minutes, at a minimum viable capacity of 50 requests per second with a 95th percentile latency of 200ms and 99th percentile latency of 500ms.
- Recovery Time Objective (RTO) for write service: 2 hours (proposed target; actual capability to be verified during the drill), measured from the controlled failure injection to sustained availability of write service with required checks passing, sustained for at least 30 minutes, at a minimum viable capacity of 20 requests per second with a 95th percentile latency of 500ms and 99th percentile latency of 1s.
- Recovery Point Objective (RPO): 1 hour, referenced to the latest acknowledged committed event before the failure, requiring a separate, verified replay source to recover intervening events.

The workload mix for read-only service will be 80% simple queries and 20% complex queries, with a maximum allowed error rate of 0.1% at the client-visible operation level. The workload mix for write service will be 50% simple writes and 50% complex writes. For write service, the error rate will be assessed statistically using a direct stratified weighted interval method with a 95% confidence level. To achieve the required sample sizes for the class-specific error limits, I will implement stratified oversampling: 60,000 simple writes and 60,000 complex writes. The aggregate error rate will be calculated by weighting the class-specific rates according to the target mix (50% simple, 50% complex), with a target upper bound of 0.0125%. Both class-specific and aggregate criteria must pass. In addition to transport errors, I will track semantic correctness separately by comparing reads and committed writes against the declared recovery watermark and state invariants. Any violations will be counted as failures. I will also test client retries across recovery to verify that they can resolve the original outcome without a duplicate effect and that restored idempotency records remain available for the full retry and replay window.
